title: Your Yard Man
sections: Up at a quarter past pitch black
Half-ton, trailer, mower on the back
Pray the reflux don't come up
I go yard to yard across your town
And I'm finished up by three
It beats a time clock forty hours
And a boss with a stopwatch on me
That's all I aim to be
And I don't mind a bit
To be plumb sick of it
My daddy punched the mill clock
They gave him a watch and a sheet cake
And a heart that wouldn't wait
He spent his last two summers
In a chair by the kitchen door
Like he never had time before
That's all I aim to be
I may never get a gold watch
Or a party when I'm through
Come Sunday I'm still up at dawn
But the mower gets a rest
Second pew in a pressed white shirt
Preacher gives us hell, God bless
Then I'm out on the lake by noon
My phone's back in the half-ton
That's all I aim to be
And I can live with that
And they'd laugh at my hat
